Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexaWave Communications Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for joining the question-and-answer session will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to NexaWave Communications' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Mark Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Harper, Chief Financial Officer; David Kim, Chief Network Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Mark Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We exceeded expectations in several key areas. First, service revenues grew robustly across wireless, broadband, and enterprise segments. Wireless rose 4.2% year-over-year, broadband 3.8%, and enterprise a strong 6.1%, reflecting our converged telecom and media momentum. Second, our operating expense management initiatives delivered substantial savings, enhancing profitability. Third, free cash flow generation was strong, supporting shareholder returns and strategic reinvestments. Fourth, network investments advanced our 5G deployment significantly. Finally, we are strategically positioning ourselves for sustained subscriber acquisition cost improvements.

Lisa Harper: Thank you, Mark. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $15.2 billion, up 4.8% year-over-year. Our adjusted EBITDA was $4.0 billion, resulting in a margin of 26.3%. We are maintaining strict cost discipline. Capital expenditures were $3.2 billion, primarily allocated to 5G rollout and fiber expansion.

Good afternoon, everyone—though it's morning here, thank you for joining our Q3 2024 earnings call. Today, I'd like to dive deep into our service revenue performance, which grew 4.7% year-over-year to $14.2 billion, marking the strongest quarterly growth in over two years and underscoring the resilience of our converged telecom and media strategy. This topline momentum was driven by balanced contributions across our core segments—wireless, broadband, and enterprise—with year-over-year growth of 4.2%, 3.8%, and 6.1%, respectively. Let me unpack each one, highlighting the key trends, operational levers, and strategic tailwinds that fueled this outperformance.

Starting with wireless service revenues, up 4.2% year-over-year to $8.9 billion. This reflects robust postpaid ARPU expansion of 2.8% to $52.34, fueled by our premium 5G Ultra Wideband tier, which now represents 68% of our postpaid phone base, up from 52% a year ago. We added 456,000 postpaid phone net adds—our best Q2 in five years—driven by strong demand for our bundled 5G Home Internet offers and partnerships like our exclusive Apple One integration, which boosted smartphone upgrades by 15% quarter-over-quarter. Churn remained industry-leading at 0.72%, below our sub-0.80% target, thanks to our AI-powered Network Intelligence platform, which dynamically optimizes spectrum allocation and reduces latency to under 10ms in 85% of our footprint.

Regionally, the Northeast and Midwest markets led with 5.1% growth, benefiting from our C-band spectrum deployment following the 2021 auction, where we secured 3.45 GHz assets ahead of peers like T-Mobile. In contrast, California saw slightly softer 3.5% growth amid competitive pricing pressures from Dish Network's 5G buildout, but our fixed wireless access ramp—now serving 1.2 million households—mitigated this, capturing 25% market share in rural overlays. Strategically, we're accelerating Open RAN trials with Nokia and Samsung, aiming for 30% of new sites by 2025, which should compress capex by 10-15% while enabling edge computing services for AR/VR media streaming. Looking ahead, we expect wireless service growth to accelerate to 5%+ in the second half as 5G SA core goes live nationwide.

Turning to broadband service revenues, which rose 3.8% year-over-year to $3.4 billion. This was anchored by our fiber-to-the-home expansion, with 1.8 million new fiber passings in the quarter, bringing our total footprint to 28 million locations—on track for 40 million by 2026. Fiber ARPA climbed 4.2% to $142, propelled by 200/200 Mbps tiers at $70/month, bundled with our NovaStream+ media service, which now has 4.5 million subscribers and drives 18% higher retention than standalone broadband. Legacy DOCSIS 3.1 revenues declined 2% as expected due to cord-cutting, but this was more than offset by FWA broadband growth of 22% YoY, adding 320,000 subscribers as a competitive alternative to Starlink in exurban markets.

Geographically, the Southeast powered 5.2% growth via our $2.5 billion RDOF commitments, where we've lit up 40% of funded locations ahead of schedule, outpacing Frontier's pace. In urban hubs like Texas and Florida, broadband penetration hit 62%, but we faced headwinds from municipal broadband initiatives in Colorado, tempering growth to 2.9%. On the media side, our integration of Peacock-like content via NovaStream+ has lifted broadband attachment rates to 35%, with average viewing hours up 12% thanks to 4K/8K streaming over DOCSIS 4.0 pilots. Our initiatives here include DOCSIS 4.0 rollouts to 5 million homes by year-end and Wi-Fi 7 gateway deployments, positioning us for symmetric gigabit demand from hyperscaler edge apps. We guide to mid-single-digit broadband growth through 2025 as fiber economics improve.

Finally, enterprise service revenues delivered standout 6.1% year-over-year growth to $2.0 billion, our fastest-growing segment and now 14% of total service mix. This was led by a 28% surge in 5G private networks and SD-WAN, with net adds of 1,200 enterprise sites, including major wins with Fortune 500 hyperscalers like AWS and media giants akin to Disney for low-latency content delivery networks. Our Private 5G ARPU jumped 9% to $18,500 per site, driven by slicing for IoT and AI workloads—think real-time analytics for stadium AR experiences or automated media production.

Regionally, international enterprise grew 12% in Europe via our Vodafone JV, focusing on mmWave campus networks, while U.S. SMB revenues expanded 7% through channel partnerships with Cisco for Meraki integrations. Large enterprise was the star at 8% growth, bolstered by our EdgeCloud platform, which reduced latency by 40% for video-on-demand workflows. Competitive dynamics favor us against Lumen's wireline declines, as our 400G fiber backbone—now spanning 75% of U.S. metros—handles surging data traffic from generative AI, up 35% YoY. Strategically, we're investing $800 million in AI-orchestrated networks with Ericsson, targeting 20% EBITDA margins in enterprise by 2026, and exploring media adjacencies like virtual production studios for Hollywood clients.

In summary, our service revenue engine is firing on all cylinders, with wireless providing scale, broadband delivering sticky household economics, and enterprise unlocking high-margin growth. These results validate our $20 billion capex plan focused on 5G, fiber, and converged media, and we remain confident in our full-year service revenue growth guidance of 4.5-5.0%.

As we dive further into the financials, I'd like to spend some time on our operating expense management initiatives, which continue to be a cornerstone of our profitability transformation. In a telecom and media landscape marked by intensifying competition from hyperscalers like Amazon and Google, rising content costs amid the streaming wars, and the massive capex demands of 5G Standalone and fiber densification, disciplined OpEx control has delivered $285 million in incremental run-rate savings year-to-date. This has directly expanded our adjusted EBITDA margin by 210 basis points to 38.2%—our highest in five years—while freeing up capital for strategic growth in edge computing and ad-supported streaming tiers.

Let me break this down by key levers, with specific impacts and regional nuances. First, network operations and IT efficiencies—our largest bucket, representing 42% of total OpEx at $2.8 billion in Q3. We've accelerated our shift to a cloud-native architecture, leveraging Software-Defined Networking and Network Function Virtualization across our 5G core. This included migrating 65% of our vRAN workloads to AWS Outposts and Azure Edge Zones, reducing hardware refresh cycles from 36 to 24 months. The result? A 15% quarter-over-quarter reduction in energy costs—saving $112 million year-to-date—driven by AI-powered predictive maintenance that cut network outages by 28% and optimized power usage effectiveness to 1.25 in our U.S. data centers.

Regionally, North America benefited most, with $78 million in savings from scale efficiencies in our Verizon-partnered Open RAN deployments in the Northeast Corridor. In EMEA, regulatory tailwinds from the EU's Gigabit Infrastructure Act allowed us to consolidate 1,200 legacy towers, yielding $45 million, though offset slightly by GDPR compliance investments. APAC remains challenged by spectrum auction costs in India, but our joint venture with Reliance Jio delivered $32 million through shared backhaul.

Second, content and programming expenses, at 28% of OpEx or $1.9 billion quarterly. Here, we've executed a portfolio rationalization inspired by peers like Disney and Warner Bros. Discovery. We divested non-core linear TV rights for $150 million in cash proceeds and pivoted to FAST channels—launching 12 new free ad-supported streaming TV services on our NovaStream platform, akin to Roku Channel or Pluto TV. This slashed acquisition costs by 22% YoY, or $167 million year-to-date, while boosting ARPU through targeted CTV ads via our integration with The Trade Desk.

In the U.S., where streaming penetration hit 85% of households, this drove 18% ad revenue growth. Europe saw $52 million savings from bundling sports rights with DAZN, navigating Ofcom regulations. However, in Latin America, inflation in Brazil pressured costs up 5%, mitigated by local content localization reducing dubbed imports by 40%.

Third, SG&A and customer operations, 30% of OpEx at $2.0 billion. Automation has been transformative: our GenAI chatbot, powered by partnerships with Google Cloud and IBM Watson, handled 72% of Tier 1 support queries—up from 45% last year—slashing call center headcount by 18%, or 4,200 FTEs, for $89 million in savings. Vendor consolidation reduced procurement spend by 12% through a master services agreement with Ericsson for OSS/BSS upgrades.

Globally, this yielded opex leverage of 1.8x revenue growth, but U.S. markets shone with $61 million from churn reduction to 1.1% monthly via hyper-personalized offers on our app. In mature markets like Japan, aging demographics increased service costs by 3%, offset by robotic process automation in billing.

Overall impact on profitability: These initiatives compressed total OpEx by 8.2% YoY to $6.7 billion, a $620 million improvement, with $285 million directly attributable to our program—exceeding our initial $250 million target. Excluding one-offs like restructuring charges, this flowed straight to the bottom line: Adjusted EBITDA rose $325 million quarter-over-quarter to $3.95 billion, with margins expanding 210bps as noted. Free cash flow hit $1.8 billion, up 35%, funding our $2.5 billion share repurchase and maintaining our leverage at 2.4x net debt to EBITDA—well within investment-grade thresholds.

Strategically, this isn't just cost-cutting; it's reallocating to high-ROI areas. We're investing $400 million of savings into 6GHz spectrum trials for Wi-Fi 7 convergence with 5G, positioning us against T-Mobile's fixed wireless aggression, and $250 million into originals for NovaStream to counter Netflix's password-sharing crackdown. Looking forward, we see another $350 million in run-rate savings by year-end 2025 from quantum-safe encryption rollouts and blockchain-based content rights management.

We're proud of this execution in a tough macro—cord-cutting at 6% annually, inflation at 4-5% on labor and energy, and capex intensity at 18% of revenue.

I'm also pleased to dive into our free cash flow performance, which remains a cornerstone of our financial strength in this capital-intensive industry. For the quarter, we generated $2.8 billion in free cash flow, up 15% year-over-year and marking our 11th consecutive quarter of FCF growth. On a trailing 12-month basis, that's $11.2 billion, putting us on track to exceed our full-year guidance midpoint of $10.5 to $11.5 billion. This robust generation underscores the maturation of our 5G Standalone core network and the synergies from our media integration post the StreamForge Entertainment acquisition.

Free cash flow is defined as adjusted operating cash flow minus capital expenditures. Our adjusted OCF came in at $4.9 billion for the quarter, a 12% increase YoY, driven by wireless segment strength: postpaid phone net adds of 450,000—our best Q3 since the pandemic—fueled by 5G Ultra Wideband penetration reaching 65% of our premium subscriber base, generating higher ARPU through fixed wireless access bundles. This mirrors Verizon's FWA momentum but with our edge in mmWave spectrum holdings from the 2021 C-band auction.

Broadband and fiber expansion contributed as residential broadband revenue grew 8%, with FTTH passings up 20% to 45 million homes, thanks to our Rural Digital Opportunity Fund wins totaling $1.2 billion. Enterprise contributions from edge computing services for hyperscalers like AWS and Azure added $250 million in high-margin recurring revenue. Media tailwinds saw NovaStream subs hit 28 million, up 25% YoY, with advertising revenue surging 35% on connected TV ad loads—benefiting from the ongoing streaming wars consolidation.

Offsetting this, capex totaled $2.1 billion, down 10% YoY as a percentage of revenue at 18%, reflecting the tail-end of our peak 5G buildout. We've shifted ~30% of RAN spend to Open RAN architectures with vendors like Nokia and Rakuten Symphony, reducing vendor lock-in and capex intensity by 15% per site. Total capex guidance remains $18-19 billion for the year.

Turning to utilization—our disciplined approach prioritizes shareholder returns while fueling growth. Of our $2.8 billion Q3 FCF: 65% or $1.8 billion returned to shareholders. We deployed $1.1 billion in dividends at our sustainable 45-50% FCF payout ratio—our quarterly dividend yield now at 4.2%. Share repurchases totaled $700 million, retiring 12 million shares or 1.5% of float under our $10 billion authorization. This accretes EPS by ~2% annually.

20% or $560 million to deleveraging: Net debt reduction brought our net leverage to 2.4x adjusted EBITDA. 15% or $440 million reinvested strategically: $250 million into content for NovaStream, securing exclusive sports rights, and the balance into R&D in 6G non-terrestrial networks with Starlink partnerships and AI-driven network slicing.

Regionally, North America generated $2.5 billion, EMEA $220 million lifted by 5G merger synergies in Germany, and APAC $80 million from joint ventures in India and Indonesia. This FCF profile de-risks our pivot to converged telecom-media. We're allocating 10-15% of future FCF to tuck-in M&A.

Looking ahead, we affirm full-year FCF guidance and see upside from FWA adoption.

I'd like to spend a few minutes on subscriber acquisition costs, or SAC, which came in at $415 per subscriber this quarter—a sequential decline of 7% from $445 in Q2 and a year-over-year improvement of 12% from $470. This marks our sixth straight quarter of SAC moderation, reflecting the maturation of our multi-product go-to-market strategy across broadband, wireless, and our NovaStream+ streaming bundle.

First, SAC dollars have stabilized below $420 for the first time since the post-pandemic surge, when costs exceeded $550 amid 5G rollout. We've clawed back over 25% through efficiencies. Marketing and advertising spend fell 15% QoQ to $158 per sub, fueled by AI-powered programmatic advertising on The Trade Desk and Google's DV360, achieving a 22% lift in efficiency using first-party data from our 45 million RGUs. We're hyper-targeting high-ARPU prospects.

Sales and distribution costs, $133 per sub, benefited from a 10% reduction in commissions and a 12% cut in retail footprint, with digital sales now 42% of acquisitions, boosted by AR virtual try-ons.

Customer premise equipment and device subsidies dropped 20% QoQ to $82 per sub. We've dialed back smartphone subsidies to $180 average, with BYOD at 35%, and FWA CPE costs down 25% via bulk deals.

In North America, SAC held at $398 per sub thanks to NovaStream+ bundling, unlocking 28% ARPU uplift. In EMEA, SAC rose to $512 from regulatory headwinds, countered by 5G fixed broadband pilots.

This underscores our 'Acquire for Life' ethos: postpaid wireless adds at $385 SAC with 0.92% churn. We guide to full-year SAC of $400-$410.

Thank you. Now, turning to our network investments, which remain the cornerstone of our long-term growth strategy in both telecommunications and media services. In Q3, we deployed $3.2 billion in capex, bringing year-to-date total to $9.8 billion—a 12% increase year-over-year, aligning with full-year guidance of $12 to $14 billion. Approximately 65%—roughly $6.4 billion YTD—has been directed toward 5G network buildout, with the balance supporting fiber backhaul, edge computing, and spectrum acquisitions. Capex as a percentage of revenue is steady at 18%, down from 20% last year.

Our 5G deployment progress continues to outpace industry benchmarks. We have 92% nationwide 5G coverage on a population basis, up from 85% year-start: 88% sub-6GHz across 2.5 GHz mid-band, and 65% mmWave in top 50 metros exceeding 1 Gbps. We've lit up over 55,000 5G sites, including 32,000 upgraded via dynamic spectrum sharing.

We're accelerating 5G Standalone, transitioning 42% of sites ahead of target, using Ericsson's RAN and Nokia's AirScale. Massive MIMO across 85% of new sites delivers 40% capacity gains. Open RAN on 15% of greenfield sites projects 20-25% opex savings.

In U.S. Northeast and California, 98% 5G SA coverage enables FWA to 1.2 million households with 25% take rates, optimizing NovaStream delivery and reducing buffering 40%. In Midwest and rural South, C-band covers 75% footprint. Internationally, Europe at 90% via Vodafone JV, APAC piloting 5G-Advanced RedCap.

These yield returns: enterprise 5G revenues up 28% to $450 million, including Universal Studios campus. Media ARPU up 6% via esports slicing. 5G subs at 55% of base, driving 4.2% ARPU increase.

We'll sustain $3.5-4 billion quarterly run-rate, shifting toward FTTx and edge data centers. These position us as 5G leader in converged services, targeting 15-20% margins from new services by 2026.

David Kim: Thank you, Lisa. I would like to provide an update on our network performance. We have made significant progress in expanding our 5G coverage to 92% nationwide, with sub-6GHz at 88% and mmWave advancing in metros. Our network reliability metrics continue to improve, with outages down 28% from AI predictive maintenance, and we are seeing increased data usage across our customer base, up 45% YoY from generative AI and streaming. We are also actively working on enhancing our cybersecurity infrastructure with quantum-safe encryption pilots. Our team's dedication to Open RAN and 5G SA rollout has been instrumental in achieving these results, enabling low-latency media services and enterprise slicing.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Alex Carter with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Alex Carter: Good morning. Can you discuss the competitive landscape and your strategy for retaining enterprise customers amid hyperscaler competition?

Mark Reynolds: Certainly, Alex. The competitive landscape in enterprise remains dynamic, with hyperscalers pushing edge services, but our strategy leverages our integrated 5G private networks and SD-WAN, which surged 28% this quarter. We've secured wins with AWS and Disney-like clients through our EdgeCloud platform, reducing latency 40% and deploying slicing for AI workloads. Our 400G fiber backbone and AI-orchestrated networks with Ericsson give us an edge over wireline peers like Lumen. We're targeting 20% EBITDA margins in enterprise by 2026 via mmWave campuses and media adjacencies like virtual studios. This converged approach ensures high retention and positions us for growth against T-Mobile and others.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jennifer Lee with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Lee: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for subscriber growth in the next quarter, and how will that impact EBITDA margins?

Lisa Harper: We anticipate continued momentum with postpaid wireless net adds around 450,000-500,000, broadband RGUs up mid-single digits from FWA and fiber, and enterprise sites adding 1,200+. This should drive service revenue growth toward 5% in Q4, supporting EBITDA margin expansion to 27%+ through OpEx leverage—another $100 million in run-rate savings—and FCF conversion above 90%. Bundles with NovaStream+ will boost ARPU, offsetting any competitive pricing while SAC stays below $410, ensuring profitability.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Wilson with Citi. Please go ahead.

Tom Wilson: Can you provide an update on your fiber deployment plans and the expected ROI on those investments?

David Kim: Absolutely, Tom. Our fiber-to-the-home expansion added 1.8 million passings this quarter, totaling 28 million on track for 40 million by 2026, complemented by FWA serving 1.2 million households. In the Southeast, we've lit 40% of RDOF locations ahead of schedule. ROI is strong: fiber ARPA up 4.2% to $142 with 18% higher retention from NovaStream bundles, and payback periods under 4 years as DOCSIS declines are offset. We're rolling out DOCSIS 4.0 to 5 million homes and Wi-Fi 7 gateways for gigabit symmetry. Combined with 5G backhaul, we expect mid-teens IRR, driving broadband growth into 2025.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Mark, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Mark Reynolds: Thank you. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value. Thank you for your time and interest in NexaWave Communications.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
